tool_input.description: Validate the pending experiment JSON parses

result:
Experiment 10 is pre-registered in `runs/pending_experiment.json`. Only that file and one design-stage probe script were written; `model/` and all frozen files are untouched.

**Design: canonical-composite reconstruction (category: loss, training-only).** Once per run, the trainer builds a fourth picture of Berlin from the three training captures only: per-survey global colour normalisation, then the per-pixel per-channel median. Because the captures are pixel-aligned, the median keeps what two or three surveys agree on and erases anything unique to one photograph (cars, one survey's shadows, one season's canopy, one year's construction, the standard DOP's leaning roofs). Each committee member gets a small throw-away decoder that must repaint the composite crop of the same position and heading at 4 m/px from the member's 8×8 feature map of its augmented own-survey view, MSE at weight 3 on top of the existing loss. The decoders are discarded before export, so the ONNX stays byte-identical at 3,942,411 bytes.

**Why this and not another invariance term.** The era's record says the problem has been the target, not the idea: exp 3's cosine was vacuous, exp 9 collapsed training outright (top1 0.008, one member constant), and exp 8's DINOv2 target was unreachable for a 1M-parameter student. A fixed pixel-space target that is survey-invariant by construction has no free optimum (chance MSE is 1.0) and no collapsed one. The probe I ran on the three training captures (never 2024) supports attainability:

| at 4 m/px, standardised crops, 300 places | correlation |
|---|---|
| survey to survey, same place | 0.58–0.62 |
| survey to composite, same place | 0.81–0.85 |
| retrieval, one survey → composite, aligned | 96–100% |

**Pre-registered expectations.** 2024 mission 1.096 → 0.96–1.06, through usable 7.5% → 10–15% and false fix 17% → 11–16%, coverage 0.245 → 0.27–0.38. Mechanical checks: per-member reconstruction MSE below 0.5 by epoch 8, member top1 within 0.05 of exp 7's 0.35, agreement ≥ 0.33. Decision rules cover a flat result (head still reads survey cues alongside the canonical structure), an unlearned target (retry at weight 10, which is safe because the term is bounded), and a coverage FAIL.

One note for the record: exp 9's FAIL was a training collapse, not a verdict on feature invariance. I wrote that into the hypothesis so the next designer does not read it as a refutation.
